metadata.case_name: CHAU SUT NGA v. HOP LEE CONSTRUCTION ENGINEERING AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: casual construction site worker, generally employed for the purpose of laying concrete

injuries.description: Moderate degrees of degenerative osteoarthritis changes in the medial and patello-femoral compartments of his right knee; permanent disability of his right knee in the way of pain, stiffness which may lead to a future operation (assessed at 6%).
source: "Radiological examinations revealed moderate degrees of degenerative osteoarthritis changes in the medial and patello-femoral compartments of his right knee. There was no evidence of old fractures nor calcifications suggestive of severe ligament injury."
"Permanent disability of his right knee in the way of pain, stiffness which may lead to a future operation was assessed at 6% (six per cent)."
Paragraph 77: "The plaintiff suffered a lasting injury to his right knee which accelerated the degenerative processes that were already underway at the time of his accident..."
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the knee or lower leg

injuries.description: Post-Concussional Syndrome (PCS) characterised by headache, dizziness, impaired concentration and memory and emotional disturbance, diagnosed as a consequence of head injury.
source: "Post-Concussional Syndrome. This is a syndrome following concussion - impairment of consciousness following a blow to head - characterized by symptoms such as headache, giddiness, impaired concentration and emotional disturbance."

"In Mr. Chau's case the features of the Syndrome are headache, dizziness, impaired concentration and memory and emotional disturbances such as irritability. The condition is moderate to severe in degree and is a consequence of the head injury caused by the accident."
Finding of Court (paragraph 74): "It has been proved, on balance, that the plaintiff suffers from PCS and DD as a direct consequence of the accident."

injuries.description: Depressive Disorder characterised by depressive mood, loss of interest and initiative, impaired mental acuity, fatiguability and impaired sleep, diagnosed as a psychological reaction to the accident and its aftermath.
source: "Depressive Disorder. This is a psychiatric disorder characterized by depressive mood and associated symptoms such as loss of interest, energy and initiative, loss of self-esteem, insomnia, poor appetite and impaired cognitive functioning."
"Depressive features in this case include depressive mood, loss of interest and initiative, impaired mental acuity, and fatiguability."
Paragraph 77: "Much more serious is that he came to acquire mental disabilities from which he is unlikely to get well, although, with treatment, there may be a partial recovery."
Finding of Court (paragraph 74): "It has been proved, on balance, that the plaintiff suffers from PCS and DD as a direct consequence of the accident."

injuries.description: Right elbow condition described in Dr Tsoi's report as 'gross destruction of the elbow joint with severe post-traumatic osteoarthritis' (defence position: unrelated to the 10 March 1991 accident).
source: "The most recent X-ray revealed gross destruction of the elbow joint with severe post-traumatic osteoarthritis."
Paragraph 75: "The existing injury to the right elbow was not caused by the accident."

"Mr. Chau has been staying in United Christian Hospital for one week after his initial admission and yet Dr. Wu in his report only mentioned that 'There are no deformity over the four limbs except the small area of abrasions over the both knees'. ... In light of all these facts, I am of the opinion that the right elbow condition is unrelated to the captioned accident." (Dr Danny Tsoi's report quoted in the judgment)
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the elbow or forearm

manifestations.description: Depressive mood, apathy, loss of interest and initiative, impaired mental acuity
Needs prompting and assistance with personal hygiene and basic tasks (e.g. bathing, shaving, cutting nails); difficulty managing own affairs
Right arm weakness, unable to extend fully

treatments_received: Admitted to United Christian Hospital for observation (kept for 7 days)
Conservative orthopaedic treatment at UCH Department of Orthopaedics until January 1993
Multiple psychiatric and neurological examinations and reports
treatments_future: Psychiatric treatment in the form of medication and psychotherapy (Dr Singer recommended 3 years at about HK$65,000 per year)
Possible future operation on right knee (may lead to a future operation) - not quantified

losses.description: Permanent disability of his right knee in the way of pain and stiffness which may lead to a future operation.
Increasing forgetfulness, slow responses, impaired concentration and memory; reduced mental acuity.
Needs prompting and assistance with personal hygiene and basic tasks; incapable of managing his own affairs.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Cannot perform simple chores like shopping for an item, cleaning around the house or preparing food.
World has shrunk to eating and sleeping, mooching around the home, seldom going out and then only when accompanied; does not engage in conversation.
Walks with a limp and usually needs support; unable to stand or walk for long periods due to right knee pain.
